data.body:
## Closing evidence — fix merged as 6546114de21a4291bb648ac52160ceea8acc403f

Gerrit change 2340 "Reclaim tagged mcp images and prove it" (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1),
merged and reachable from origin/main. Verified against a fresh worktree detached at
origin/main (25ea12c200ae), which contains the merge. All six acceptance criteria are
codebase-verifiable; none required a `[non-codebase]` provenance tag, and no read or
mutation was performed on box i-00880b2c7f13527c5.

Full affected suite: 66 passed (tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py,
tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_disk_pressure.py,
tests/scripts/test_observability_disk_pressure.py, tests/unit/test_autodeploy_prune.py).

### AC1 — reaped container's `compose-mcp:<sha>` removed; live image + bare build tag retained
`mcp_retire_sweep` (autodeploy.sh) reads `docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Image}}'` BEFORE the
`docker rm` (unreadable afterwards; the container name carries only a truncated sha + port, so
it can never be string-manipulated into a tag) and calls `mcp_retire_image` only inside the
`if docker rm …; then` success branch.
Tests: `test_reaping_a_drained_container_retires_its_per_release_image` (live `compose-mcp:aaa…`
+ exited `compose-mcp:bbb…`; asserts removals == exactly `[compose-mcp:bbb…]`),
`test_the_bare_build_tag_is_never_retired`, `test_an_image_shared_with_the_live_backend_is_retained`.

### AC2 — a serving container's image is NEVER removed (the dangerous one)
Structurally, removal lives ONLY in the not-running branch of `mcp_retire_sweep`, gated on the
`docker rm` succeeding. Three independent guards in `mcp_retire_image`: bare `$MCP_IMAGE`
(+`:latest`/`:prev`) skipped, the live backend's image skipped, and `docker image rm` run
WITHOUT `-f` so the daemon refuses while any container still references the image.
Test: `test_a_running_containers_image_is_never_removed` seeds a live container on 8092
(`compose-mcp:aaa…`) and a still-RUNNING draining one on 8091 with in_flight=3
(`compose-mcp:ccc…`) — the case where serving and reaped differ only by TAG — and asserts the
draining container is stopped, no image removal is issued, AND no `image-rm-refused` appears,
so the guarantee is the reap ordering itself and not a rescue by the daemon's refusal.

NOT VACUOUS — proven by mutation, each reverted immediately (worktree left clean):
* Deleting the live-image guard in `mcp_retire_image` ->
  `test_an_image_shared_with_the_live_backend_is_retained` FAILS
  ("no removal may even be ATTEMPTED for the live backend's image").
* Adding `mcp_retire_image` to the still-RUNNING (`mcp_retire_graceful`) branch ->
  `test_a_running_containers_image_is_never_removed` FAILS
  ("the guard must be the reap ordering itself").
The docker stub models the real daemon: `image rm` without `-f` exits 1 and logs
`image-rm-refused` while any container still references the image, so the third guard is
exercised rather than assumed.

### AC3 — `prune_docker_caches` logs free space before, after, and the delta
`root_disk_free_kb()` (the `df --output=avail /` sibling of `root_disk_pct`, echoing 0 on an
unparseable probe) is read before and after the prunes, then
`log "prune_docker_caches: root-disk free before=…kB after=…kB freed=…kB"`.
Test: `test_pressure_reclaim_logs_free_space_before_after_and_the_delta` asserts the literal
`before=10000kB after=60000kB freed=50000kB` and `root disk 90% -> 40%`.

### AC4 — streak counter across pressure / throttle / relief
Three tick outcomes, one rule each. The RESET sits before `reclaim_under_pressure`'s
below-threshold early return (a recovered tick never reaches the post-reclaim code, so a reset
placed there would be unreachable); the throttled branch returns before the counter code, so a
throttled tick leaves it unchanged; a completed reclaim re-reads `root_disk_pct()` and
increments if still `>= DISK_PRESSURE_PCT`, else resets. Persisted at `PRESSURE_STREAK_FILE`
under `$STATE_DIR` with tmp+rename; reads fail safe toward silence (absent/non-numeric = 0).
Tests: `test_streak_increments_when_a_reclaim_leaves_the_disk_pressured`,
`test_streak_resets_to_zero_once_the_disk_falls_below_the_threshold`,
`test_a_reclaim_that_recovers_the_disk_clears_the_streak`,
`test_a_throttled_pressured_tick_leaves_the_streak_unchanged`,
`test_a_corrupt_streak_file_fails_safe_toward_silence`.

### AC5 — distinct marker at `PRESSURE_STREAK_ALARM` (default 3), published as its own metric
`marker AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE_PERSISTS reclaim-ineffective …` fires at
`streak >= PRESSURE_STREAK_ALARM`; observability.sh publishes
`'^AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE_PERSISTS \{'` as `disk_pressure_persists` with its own offset file.
Tests: `test_persistence_marker_fires_at_the_third_consecutive_ineffective_cycle` is a genuine
THRESHOLD test — cycles 1 and 2 emit NOTHING, cycle 3 emits exactly one marker carrying
`"reason": "reclaim-ineffective"`; `test_the_alarm_threshold_is_configurable` lowers the tunable
to 1 and the FIRST cycle alarms; `test_the_persistence_marker_is_distinct_from_the_invocation_counter`
plus `test_the_two_disk_pressure_counters_never_cross_count` prove the record-anchored patterns
cannot cross-count despite one token being a strict prefix of the other.
NOT VACUOUS — replacing `-ge "$PRESSURE_STREAK_ALARM"` with `-ge 1` fails three tests
(threshold, negative control, corrupt-counter). Reverted.

### AC6 — fires only on PERSISTENCE (negative control)
`test_a_single_pressured_cycle_that_recovers_never_emits_the_marker`: one pressured cycle
(streak 1, no marker), then relief -> no marker and streak back to 0. At the metric layer,
`test_no_persistence_markers_publishes_zero` publishes 0 for a box whose reclaims all worked.
Together with AC5's mutation result, the alarm is proven two-sided: it fires at the threshold
and does not fire below it.
